title: Pump moved from throttling to a variable speed drive, with site constants
grade: First draft on site constants: every constant is a site value, but the measured inputs are as entered and have not been checked against a representative period.
assumptions: Pump P-101 on a variable speed drive: the kW figures are the average load over the whole year's running, at the same production rate before and after, not a single spot reading.
Pump P-101 on a variable speed drive: the change applies for 8,000 h/yr.
Pump P-101 on a variable speed drive: one energy price applies to every kWh saved (no time-of-use periods, tiers or riders).
Pump P-101 on a variable speed drive: the demand reduction lowers the billing peak in each of 12 months, which happens only if the load is reduced at the time of the peak.
Pump P-101 on a variable speed drive: Scope 2 uses a grid average (location-based) factor; the generation that actually backs off at the margin can emit more or less.
Where a range is entered, the result carries both ends. That is the spread of what was entered, not a probability interval.
to_firm_up: Confirm by measurement: Average electrical input kW before and after (or the kW reduction): a clamp-on three-phase power meter, the drive or MCC power reading, or the historian's motor kW tag, over a representative period at the same production rate. An estimate from curves (pump/fan curve and affinity laws) must say so.
Confirm by measurement: Operating hours per year the change applies: historian run status, the operating schedule, or maintenance records. Not 8,760 unless it really runs all year.
Confirm by measurement: Optional: the reduction in billing-peak kW (interval meter data at the billing interval) and the months it applies.
After the change, measure the same quantities again at the same production rate: that before/after pair, not this estimate, is the saving.

electricity_price_per_kwh.label: site value: ILLUSTRATIVE energy charge from a made-up rate schedule

grid_kg_co2e_per_kwh.label: site value: ILLUSTRATIVE subregion factor (look yours up in EPA Power Profiler)

demand_charge_per_kw_month.label: site value: ILLUSTRATIVE demand charge from the same made-up rate schedule

changes.change: Pump P-101 on a variable speed drive

steps.formula: billing-peak kW reduction x demand charge x months

limits: An estimate from the inputs shown, not a measured or verified saving. It is only as good as the measured kW, flow and hours; a before/after measurement at the same production rate is the proof.
Electricity cost uses one energy price per kWh. Tariffs vary (time-of-use, tiers, riders, power factor); demand charges count only when the reduction lowers the billing peak.

Electricity CO2e is location-based Scope 2 (grid average factor given). Market-based Scope 2 uses your supplier's factor or contract instruments and can differ greatly; avoided emissions on the margin also differ.
No savings come from a drawing alone: every quantity here was measured or supplied by the user.
